description: Tsunami Simulations in Support of California’s Fifth Climate Change Assessment is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "simulation", published or maintained by Patrick Lynett, University of Southern California (usc.edu). This project evaluates how future sea-level rise may alter tsunami inundation hazards along the California coast. It contains numerical tsunami-modeling data for eight representative study areas, Crescent City, Humboldt Bay, Alameda/Contra Costa, Pillar Point, Santa Cruz, Ventura, the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, and San Diego. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "simulation" project. Keywords: tsunami, sea-level rise, inundation hazards, California coast, probabilistic tsunami hazard, numerical tsunami modeling. Published 2026-08-01. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
